title: BlogEp 104: From $2,000 to $1 Million – Matthew Monaco’s Road to Trading Success
description: Hear how Matthew Monaco turned a $2,000 investment and early failures into multimillion-dollar success!
body_content:
Matthew Monaco: From $2,000 to Millions – A Trader’s Journey

Matthew Monaco’s journey into trading is a story of persistence and transformation. Starting in 2017 as a college student studying software engineering, Matthew wasn’t satisfied with the idea of a traditional 9-to-5 career. After a few internships and realizing that a corporate job wasn’t for him, he turned to trading with just $2,000 in savings. His first year was tough, making every mistake in the book and ultimately losing it all.

However, Matthew didn’t give up and his fortunes began to change. His account grew quickly, reaching millions as he capitalized on the market chaos from the covid pandemic.

Today, Matthew continues to trade, but his strategy has evolved. His success is a testament to the power of persistence, constant learning, and adapting to market changes.For aspiring traders, Matthew’s story proves that patience and discipline can turn early setbacks into long-term success.

Listen in to learn more!
guest_name: From $2,000 to $1 Million – Matthew Monaco’s Road to Trading Success

title: BlogEP 102: Turning $2K into $1.6 MILLION with Eduardo Briceño
description: Ian Ostrosky, health coach at Marek Health, joins The Wall Street Coach to discuss the newly launched Optimize Trader Bundle. He's passionate about contributing to a much needed paradigm shift in how we approach disease prevention, health optimization, and human performance.
body_content:
The Journey of Building a Trading Community: Managing Expectations and Overcoming Challenges

Eduardo Briceño’sjourney in the trading world began in 2018, when a small group of Spanish-speaking traders started collaborating. By 2019, they had decided to take things more seriously, and that’s when their trading community truly began to take shape. Fast forward five years, and today they have a global network of nearly 300 traders. It’s an impressive feat, but as Eduardo shared in our conversation, building this community—and succeeding in the trading world—has been anything but easy.

One of the most important lessons Eduardo has learned along the way is the crucial role that managing expectations plays in success.

Eduardo explained how, in the early years, he fell into the trap of expecting immediate success. He even made spreadsheets predicting his potential earnings, but quickly learned that trading, like any business, requires patience and resilience.

Ultimately, Eduardo’s message is clear: success in trading is a marathon, not a sprint. By focusing on building solid foundations, managing expectations, and embracing the ups and downs, traders can gradually find their way to long-term success. “It’s not about making money right away,” he said, “it’s about treating trading like a business, staying consistent, and weathering the storm.”

Instagram –@edu_trades

title: BlogEP 101: How To Biohack Your Trading
description: Ian Ostrosky, health coach at Marek Health, joins The Wall Street Coach to discuss the newly launched Optimize Trader Bundle. He's passionate about contributing to a much needed paradigm shift in how we approach disease prevention, health optimization, and human performance.
body_content:
This episode of The Wall Street Coach has Ian Ostrosky, business development manager atMarek Health, joining us to discuss the newly launchedOptimize Trader Bundle. Ian is passionate about contributing to a much needed paradigm shift in how we approach disease prevention, health optimization, and human performance. He and his team look forward to collaborating with traders and investors so they can up level their PnL by focusing on their health AND their hormones– addressing the unique physiological and mental needs of traders.

So, why should traders focus on their health? The answer lies in the critical relationship between hormones and cognitive performance. Research indicates that hormones like testosterone can significantly influence trading success. Higher testosterone levels are linked to enhanced judgment, risk tolerance, and confidence—essential qualities for effective trading.

Traders often operate under high stress, which can lead to imbalances in hormone levels. This is where regular lab work comes into play. By monitoring hormone profiles, traders can gain valuable insights into how their physical health affects their trading performance. Understanding markers like testosterone, thyroid function, and metabolic health can help traders optimize their mental game and improve decision-making skills.

Optimizing hormone levels isn’t a magic solution, but it offers a VALUABLE TOOL for traders looking to enhance their performance sustainably.

Join us as we explore how prioritizing health can transform your trading journey! By investing in your well-being, you not only improve your trading outcomes, but also enjoy a healthier, more balanced life.

description: Listen as Kim Ann Curtin sits down with trader, investor, market analyst, and expert commentator, Danielle Shay.
body_content:
In this episode of The Wall Street Coach Podcast, Kim Ann Curtin sits down with trader, investor, market analyst, and expert commentator,Danielle Shay. Danielleis VP of Options atSimpler Trading, where she runs trades and analysis in the trading room, teaches classes and webinars, and writes. You can also find Danielle regularly in the media, as she is an expert guest on CNBC, Fox News, TraderTV Live, Stockcharts, and more.

Danielle shares her unique journey into the world of trading, which began unexpectedly when her father introduced her to options trading as a way to support her family after becoming a single mom.Initially planning on law school, Danielle’s path changed when she started teaching English in Costa Rica. However, the birth of her son and the need for financial stability led her to explore other avenues. Skeptical at first, she began learning options trading online while juggling the challenges of single motherhood.

Danielle admits the early years were tough, especially since she didn’t have a strong background in math or science. Instead, she focused on recognizing patterns and applying that skill to technical analysis, which became her breakthrough. Danielle shares the method that allowed her to remove emotions from her trading decisions, making her approach more systematic and disciplined.

Danielle’s story is one of perseverance and determination. For two years, Danielle struggled and even considered giving up, but thanks to the support of her father and mentors, she pushed through and eventually found success.

title: BlogEP 97: Why Most Traders Fail at Risk Management
description: In this podcast episode, Kim Ann Curtin welcomes back Brian Lee to discuss the often misunderstood concept of risk in trading, emphasizing its importance for both novice and experienced traders.
body_content:
In this episode of The Wall Street Coach Podcast, host Kim Ann Curtinwelcomes back trading expert Brian Leeto tackle “Common Misconceptions About Risk.” Brian, a seasoned trader, delves into the pervasive myth that to make a lot, one must risk a lot. He emphasizes that risk is an ever-present factor, regardless of a trader’s experience level. Brian explains how improper risk management, such as risking large percentages of one’s account on a single trade, can lead to significant losses that are hard to recover from due to the concept of geometric returns and losses.

He advocates for consistent position sizing, highlighting that even risking a small percentage like 1% can reliably compound over time without exposing the trader to devastating losses. This episode sheds light on the importance of sticking to a well-thought-out risk management strategy, even during winning streaks, to avoid the pitfalls of overconfidence. Brian also reflects on his own journey, recognizing the critical importance of risk management early in his career, a lesson he shares to help both novice and experienced traders navigate the complexities of trading. This discussion is a must-listen for anyone looking to enhance their trading strategy and safeguard their investments.

Check out another interview with Brianhere.

title: BlogEp 90: Don’t Let Your Mind Sabotage Your Trading: Master the Mental Game of Trading with Steven Goldstein
description: Steven Goldstein joins The Wall Street Coach podcast and explores the transformative journey of becoming a consistently successful trader, shedding light on the often-overlooked elements of vulnerability and purpose.
body_content:
Unlocking Trading Success withSteven Goldstein:The Power of Vulnerability and Purpose

In the fast-paced world of trading, success often hinges on a delicate balance of skills, mindset, and adaptability. As traders, we navigate the unpredictable market terrain, facing both triumphs and challenges. In this podcast episode, we explore the transformative journey of becoming a consistently successful trader, shedding light on the often-overlooked elements of vulnerability and purpose.

Embracing Vulnerability: A Game-Changer in Trading

Imagine a scenario where stress is a constant companion, and success is marked by the ability to navigate through the highs and lows of the market. This is the reality for many traders, and it was no different for one individual who went from being a hesitant trader to achieving sustainable success.

In a candid conversation, Steven Goldstein reflects on the transformation that happened when he embraced vulnerability and sought the guidance of a coach. Trading is inherently stressful, but learning to live with and manage that stress became a game-changer. His journey mirrors the experiences of many in the financial world who grapple with the idea of seeking external help for personal development.

Resistance to help is not uncommon in the finance industry. The perception of needing external support can challenge one’s confidence, which is particularly prevalent among high-performing individuals. However, Steven’s story takes a positive turn as he recounts discovering the power of vulnerability. Acknowledging the need for support, opening up to coaching, and embracing vulnerability became pivotal in his journey toward sustained success.

Steven Goldstein is renowned as a top performance coach within the financial market, known for his expertise in guiding individuals involved in trading and investment activities towards enhanced performance and capability. With nearly 25 years of experience in senior trading roles in London’s Rates and FX markets, Steven brings a wealth of insight into the complexities of financial markets and human behavior under risk. He is co-host of The AlphaMind Podcast and his new book, Mastering the Mental Game of Trading, is out now.

title: BlogEp 88: Reminiscences of a Day Trader with David S. Hale
description: In this episode, David Hale talks about the harsh realities of day trading and what traders can expect if they choose to pursue a career in day trading.
body_content:
So, you’ve probably heard all the success stories of traders living the high life. But let’s get real – trading isn’t just about cashing in on big wins. In a recent chat, David S. Hale talks about the not-so-glamorous side of a 23-year career in the industry.

We all go through it – those moments of shame, disappointment, and frustration. David digs deep into the struggles, calling out the stigma around shame that keeps traders from being real about their journey. He’s all about embracing vulnerability, believing it’s the key to letting others know they’re not alone in their struggle.

The conversation gets into the nitty-gritty of why traders find it tough to share their struggles with friends and family. Turns out, losses hit differently in the trading world. It’s not like your regular 9-to-5 where a bad day doesn’t mean your whole life is falling apart.

David doesn’t hold back on the personal stuff, sharing tales of relationship drama and financial hits. He talks about how trading can get toxic and advises traders to build a support system. Lesson learned – don’t go it alone.

One big takeaway? Always have a Plan B. David wishes he had a safety net during the rough times. So, if you’re thinking of diving into trading, stash some savings or have a side hustle ready. It’s like having a financial cushion when the market throws a curveball.

The interview takes on the full-time versus part-time trading debate. David gets it – to be a trading pro requires serious dedication, but he’s not blind to the fact that bills need paying!

Listen in to get David’s perspective on the emotional and practical sides of trading! It’s not just about charts and graphs; it’s about bouncing back from losses, keeping it real, and having a solid plan for when the going gets tough.

description: Kim speaks with Thomas Vozzo, CEO of Homeboy Industries, about his radical approach to leadership and life. Prepare to be inspired!
body_content:
Thomas Vozzo is an author, social enterprise builder and thought leader. He’s also the CEO ofHomeboy Industries, an organization that The Wall Street Coach Podcast host Kim Ann Curtin has supported for years. In this conversation, he and Kim talk about his radical approach to leadership — and life!

Thomas Vozzo was a successful corporate leader with a reputation for results. But decades into his career, he began to feel like something was missing – a thought that would eventually lead him to become the Chief Executive Officer at Homeboy Industries, the largest gang rehabilitation and re-entry program in the world. For more than 34 years, Homeboy Industries has been a beacon of hope in Los Angeles, providing training and support to formerly gang-involved and previously incarcerated individuals, helping them to heal and redirect their lives.

A decade into his executive leadership role at Homeboy Industries – Vozzo is also the author of “The Homeboy Way: A Radical Approach to Leadership and Life.” Written with heartfelt authenticity and purpose, Vozzo invites corporate America and leaders everywhere to create a new bottom line, challenge the corporate status quo – and combat injustice, economic and racial inequity.

In his free time, Thomas enjoys hiking, ocean swimming, travelling, and spending time with his family.
